findings.title: Stateful destructive-change classification does not use the canonical service selection
Forgejo VM images can be downloaded without checksum verification
Parallel Ansible waves do not serialize services that share one host
Canonical service-state backup and restore is broken across selection, inputs, and documentation
Fresh-site onboarding has a circular validation dependency
Tailscale canonical enablement is silently double-gated
Pre-mutation secret preflight omits required host-identity secrets
Documented teardown bypasses saved-plan identity and freshness controls
Hermes Control authenticated readiness always sends a malformed bearer token
Canonical secret namespaces and migration targets contradict runtime consumers
Runtime artifact installation is not consistently immutable
Apply verification has a mutation-time TOCTOU window
`site.yml` is a misleading, incomplete, unconditional orchestration surface
Public validation is sensitive to ignored local Markdown files
Local OpenTofu state has no locking or documented single-writer control
Ansible lint globally disables the principal command-idempotence rule
Operator password hashing is not idempotent and root salts are globally reused
OpenTofu validation is inconsistent across service-specific inputs
The OpenTofu root contract remains a large compatibility surface
Supply-chain controls stop short of immutable base/container inputs and automated scanning
Canonical update behavior contradicts update policy
Site-local SOPS recipient policy verification can fail open
Every service subprocess receives the bootstrap root password
Restore can report success after service restart failures
Sensitive Ansible role arguments are inconsistently protected
Check-mode and task-tag contracts are absent, and the static checker is inaccurate
Stateful retention policy exists only in wrappers
Arbitrary override maps rely on secret-looking key names
Python quality and coverage are largely ungated
Role interface contracts are incomplete
Documentation lacks a complete service-by-service operations matrix
Documentation link checks validate paths but not anchors or executable snippets
CI validates only main pushes and pull requests
Aggregate local validation gives little failure-stage summary
Copied scaffold README links resolve outside the private values repository
Documentation inventory conflates active truth with unfinished design material
Provider compatibility is broader than the reviewed pre-1.0 series
Tooling architecture and host prerequisites are not declared

evidence.boundary: Disposable development plan review only; no apply performed. Fresh plans before convergence and after recovery were zero-change with no destructive changes.
Reviewed disposable development apply only; no isolated-recovery or production acceptance.

Development guests only across two full convergence passes plus direct-service connectivity; nonzero changes limited to the accepted imperative-bootstrap exceptions recorded in docs/governance/validation-findings-2026-08-22.md, including the sssf pinned-checkout changed_when declaration; Technitium DNS sync verified zero-change after the rData matching fix.

Enabled development stateful services only; not controller or infrastructure recovery. All enabled services backed up and restored with automatic pre-restore safety archives and zero failures; post-restore connectivity and reconvergence passed.

Disposable development controller/infrastructure recovery rehearsal on a local-filesystem host: guarded audit-journal and state snapshots were created, verified, and restored through the site lock inside one wrapped tooling session; canonical projections verified afterward followed by a fresh zero-change plan and connectivity pass. No external durability claim.

Deployed-plugin read-only status and audit verification only: zero-change non-destructive saved plan reported and audit chain verified with no unresolved correlations. It does not establish authenticated dashboard/API or WebSocket acceptance, external audit durability, mutation approval identity, rollback, isolated-recovery, or production acceptance.

Disposable development Hermes managed-release rollback rehearsal only: an intentionally invalid activation entered the guarded rescue path, restored the prior managed venv link, restarted gateway and dashboard, verified local gateway/dashboard health, and was followed by a zero-change provider plan. It does not establish rollback for other services, isolated-recovery, external audit durability, or production acceptance.
